report.source_text: On examination, the patient had difficulty lifting the left arm, a left Horner’s pupil with mild ptosis and miosis, loss of temperature sensation on the right side of the body, and numbness on the left side of the face and right side of the body. The patient had a negative skew test and no swelling or trauma to the extremities. Deep tendon reflexes were absent in the lower extremities. NIH stroke score (NIHSS) upon presentation was determined to be a three (minor severity) based on left upper extremity motor drift and sensory deficit, and blurred vision (diplopia).

clinician.final_diagnosis: 4 mm acute left lateral medullary infarct of the left posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) vascular territory
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old patient with multiple vascular risk factors (hypertension, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus type 2, hypercholesterolemia, chronic kidney disease 3a, HIV, late-stage syphilis, coronary artery disease s/p CABG×3, aortic stenosis s/p mechanical valve) presented to the ED after awakening from sleep with acute left-sided hemiparesis, paresthesias, diminished sensation, ataxic gait, and left craniofacial pain. Neurological examination revealed classic Wallenberg syndrome features: left Horner's syndrome (ptosis and miosis), ipsilateral left facial sensory loss, contralateral right-sided temperature sensation loss, left upper extremity motor weakness, and absent lower extremity deep tendon reflexes. NIHSS score was 3 (minor severity). Brain MRI on hospital day 2 confirmed a 4 mm acute left lateral medullary infarct in the left PICA vascular territory. Vascular imaging (CTA and carotid ultrasound) showed 50% right internal carotid artery stenosis but no large vessel disease or intracranial stenosis explaining the acute PICA infarct. A concerning CT finding of right frontoparietal temporal hypodensity on day 2 was ruled out by MRI. The patient's left-sided strength improved to 3-4/5 by hospital day 3. Patient was discharged on hospital day 4 on warfarin 7.5 mg daily with meclizine for dizziness and recommendations for physical and occupational therapy with a front wheel walker.
